title: Restriction of formal coherent modules is exact; exactness is local
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] whose underlying space is quasi-compact) and $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals; $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is the category of [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian], with exactness as in [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. (1) For every open $U\subseteq X$, $U$ (with $\mathcal O_X|_U$) is a Noetherian scheme, $\mathcal I|_U\subseteq\mathcal O_U$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals, and the restriction $\rho_U:\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)\to\mathit{Coh}(U,\mathcal I|_U)$, $(\mathcal F_n)\mapsto(\mathcal F_n|_U)$, $(\alpha_n)\mapsto(\alpha_n|_U)$, is a well-defined additive functor which is exact: it carries every short exact sequence of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ to a short exact sequence of $\mathit{Coh}(U,\mathcal I|_U)$. (2) Let $X=\bigcup_{j\in J}U_j$ be an open covering and $\mathcal A\xrightarrow{\beta}\mathcal B\xrightarrow{\alpha}\mathcal C$ morphisms of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ with $\alpha\circ\beta=0$. Then the sequence is exact at $\mathcal B$ if and only if for every $j$ the sequence $\rho_{U_j}(\mathcal A)\to\rho_{U_j}(\mathcal B)\to\rho_{U_j}(\mathcal C)$ is exact at $\rho_{U_j}(\mathcal B)$ in $\mathit{Coh}(U_j,\mathcal I|_{U_j})$; in particular $0\to\mathcal A\to\mathcal B\to\mathcal C\to0$ is a short exact sequence of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ if and only if $0\to\rho_{U_j}(\mathcal A)\to\rho_{U_j}(\mathcal B)\to\rho_{U_j}(\mathcal C)\to0$ is a short exact sequence of $\mathit{Coh}(U_j,\mathcal I|_{U_j})$ for every $j$.

proof.text: Prove local detection of zero objects: if the restricted object is zero on every member of the cover, evaluation of its inclusion is zero at every level. Thus the restricted zero endomorphism is an isomorphism levelwise. Apply the existing isomorphism-local theorem to the global zero endomorphism. A zero endomorphism is invertible only on a zero object.

lean.statement: theorem coherentFormalModules_local_exactness (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData) : ∃ (hN : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsNoetherian U.toScheme) (ρ : ∀ U : X.Opens, CoherentFormalModule X I ⥤ @CoherentFormalModule U.toScheme (hN U) (I.comap U.ι)) (hz : ∀ U : X.Opens, (ρ U).PreservesZeroMorphisms), (∀ U : X.Opens, (ρ U).Additive ∧ ρ U ⋙ (IsCoherentFormalModule (I.comap U.ι)).ι = (IsCoherentFormalModule I).ι ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ X.Modules U.toScheme.Modules).obj (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι) ∧ ∀ S : ShortComplex (CoherentFormalModule X I), S.ShortExact → (@ShortComplex.map _ _ _ _ _ _ S (ρ U) (hz U)).ShortExact) ∧ (∀ (J : Type v) (U : J → X.Opens), iSup U = ⊤ → ∀ S : ShortComplex (CoherentFormalModule X I), (S.Exact ↔ ∀ j : J, (@ShortComplex.map _ _ _ _ _ _ S (ρ (U j)) (hz (U j))).Exact) ∧ (S.ShortExact ↔ ∀ j : J, (@ShortComplex.map _ _ _ _ _ _ S (ρ (U j)) (hz (U j))).ShortExact))
